title: macOS older than Apple's latest security update, and fixes for exploited flaws (CVE-2026-86950 and others)
summary: Apple's latest security releases for the Mac, as its index listed them on 13 Nov 2026, are macOS Golden Gate 27.2.1, Tahoe 26.7.3 and Sequoia 15.8.3 (all 9 Nov 2026); macOS Sonoma 14's last is 14.8.9 (6 Aug 2026). Three flaws Apple fixed are in CISA's catalog of exploited vulnerabilities: CVE-2026-86950, an out-of-bounds write in CoreGraphics, which the CVE record lists as fixed in macOS 26.7.1 and 15.8.1 and for which it names no Sonoma fix; CVE-2026-65400, a Screen Sharing authentication bypass, fixed in 27, 26.6.1, 15.7.9 and 14.8.9; and CVE-2024-27834, fixed in macOS 14.5 (and Safari 17.5). A Mac below the fix for one of these on its own line is EXPOSED. One past them but below its line's latest release is REVIEW. Every Sonoma 14 is REVIEW: Apple ships it no more updates and does not say it is affected. A beta of the next release carries that release's number, so a would-be SAFE on a beta build (ProductBuildVersion ending in a lowercase letter, as 27.3 beta 1's 26C5035r of 3 Nov does), or on a build that can't be read, is REVIEW. Wardlatch reads the version and the build from /System/Library/CoreServices/SystemVersion.plist; it runs no program.

macosLines.frozen: Apple has published no security update for macOS Sonoma 14 since 14.8.9 on 6 Aug 2026; its releases of 9 Nov 2026 are for macOS 27, 26 and 15. The CVE record of CVE-2026-86950, which CISA lists as exploited, names fixes for macOS 26 and 15 and none for Sonoma. It does not say Sonoma is affected, so this is not judged EXPOSED; but this Mac no longer gets Apple's fixes

olderNote: Apple's security releases of 9 Nov 2026 are for macOS 27, 26 and 15 only, and the CVE records of the exploited CVE-2026-86950 and CVE-2026-65400 name no fix for macOS 13 or older. They do not say this release is affected, so it is not judged EXPOSED; but this Mac no longer gets Apple's fixes
olderFix: Move this Mac to a macOS Apple still updates (27, 26 or 15) if it can run one: System Settings, General, Software Update. If it can't, keep it off untrusted networks and away from untrusted files and web pages.
fix: Update macOS to {release} or later: System Settings, General, Software Update.
fixBeta: Install the release (System Settings, General, Software Update): Apple's security notes are for its releases, not its betas. If you keep a beta, update it to the newest one.
fixFrozen: Apple ships no more updates for macOS Sonoma: update to {release}, its last, if this Mac is below it, and move to a macOS Apple still updates (27, 26 or 15) if this Mac can run one (System Settings, General, Software Update).
notCovered: Rapid Security Responses and Safari, which Apple can update apart from macOS (CVE-2024-27834 is also fixed in Safari 17.5); other Apple devices; and any Apple fix not yet in its security releases index.
